outputs.justification: The manuscript cites TargetScan (https://www.targetscan.org/vert_80/) as the in‑silico miRNA target prediction resource. The URL is valid and resolves to the TargetScan release 8.0 search page (miRNA target prediction/search interface) where predicted targets can be queried and downloaded. ([targetscan.org](https://www.targetscan.org/vert_80/?utm_source=openai))

The manuscript states: “The RNA‑seq data have been deposited in the BioStudies database under accession number S-BSST2081.” No explicit BioStudies URL was given in the text. I attempted to locate a public BioStudies landing page for accession S-BSST2081 but could not find a publicly accessible study page for that accession via standard BioStudies patterns/search. Possible explanations: (a) the accession is embargoed/private and not yet publicly released, (b) the accession contains a typographical error, or (c) the authors neglected to provide the direct public URL. BioStudies uses study landing pages (e.g., https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/studies/<ACCESSION>); if the study is public this URL normally resolves to a page listing the files/metadata. I recommend the authors provide the direct BioStudies landing-page URL (or correct accession) or confirm public release so reviewers/readers can access the RNA‑seq data. ([ebi.ac.uk](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/about?utm_source=openai))
